preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(t, str) for t in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Each test case is a non-empty string composed of uppercase letters 'A'-'Z' and/or '?'

preconditions.expression: all(len(t) >= 1 and len(t) <= 2013 for t in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Each test case string has length between 1 and 2013, inclusive

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ?' for c in t) for t in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Each character in every test case string is either an uppercase letter or '?'
The number of test cases T is between 1 and 2013, inclusive

postconditions.description: The result contains exactly one output string per test case

postconditions.expression: all(len(result[i]) == len(test_cases[i]) for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: Each output string has the same length as its corresponding input string

postconditions.expression: all(all(c in 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ' for c in result[i]) for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: Each output string contains only uppercase letters (no '?')

postconditions.expression: all(all(result[i][j] == test_cases[i][j] or test_cases[i][j] == '?' for j in range(len(test_cases[i]))) for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: Each output string preserves the original non-'?' characters from the input

postconditions.expression: all(any(all(result[i][k:k+4] == 'CHEF' for k in range(len(result[i])-3)) == max(any(all(s[k:k+4] == 'CHEF' for k in range(len(s)-3)) for s in possible_strings(test_cases[i])) for i in range(T)))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string maximizes the number of 'CHEF' substrings, where possible_strings(s) is the set of all strings obtainable by replacing '?' in s with uppercase letters

postconditions.expression: all(result[i] == min([s for s in possible_strings(test_cases[i]) if count_chef(s) == max_count(test_cases[i])]) for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: Among all strings with the maximum number of 'CHEF' substrings, the output string is lexicographically smallest, where count_chef(s) is the number of 'CHEF' substrings in s and max_count(s) is the maximum count_chef over all possible strings for s
